note: Ground truth for the eval harness. Never readable by packages/agents, packages/store or apps/server. Times are virtual microseconds from simulation start. Replay outcomes are what the simulator produced on seeds 42, 3 and 7; see NOTES.md, Phase 6 (Scenario C).

rootCause.summary: The inventory v1.9.0 deploy changed the stock cache key; the hit ratio collapsed and the stock reads fell through to the database, which saturated.
rootCause.resource: inventory stock cache (and, as a consequence, the DB executor)
rootCause.mechanism: inventory looks stock up through a 20,000-entry cache over about 21,000 keys (about 95 % hits). v1.9.0 adds warehouse and customer segment to the key: about 400,000 keys, a new key format (every cached entry is useless at once), and even a full cache holds 5 % of them. Nearly every stock lookup now runs two DB queries; the database (16 parallel queries) saturates, queries queue while holding connections, the pool fills with busy connections, and latency climbs for everything that touches the database; checkout runs out of workers and rejects some requests.

causalChain.step: inventory v1.9.0 deployed: stock cache keyed by warehouse and customer segment
inventory cache hit ratio falls from about 95 % to about 5 %
the DB executor saturates (16 of 16, queue about 14); the pool fills with busy connections
stock and checkout latency climb; checkout's workers fill and it rejects some requests

discriminatingEvidence: inventory cache_hit_ratio drops right after the deploy, against a steady baseline
the pool is saturated but its connections are busy executing or queued at the DB (not idle-held): not hold-and-wait
per-query execution time is flat; the time goes to waiting for a connection and in the DB executor queue: not a slower database
the DB receives far more queries than at baseline while traffic at the gateway is unchanged

redHerrings.whyNotCausal: The same service as the real cause, 3.5 minutes earlier; no request comes near either limit; reverting it changes nothing.

redHerrings.what: payment provider latency blip at T+7:00

rejectedAlternatives.hypothesis: the connection pool is too small
rejectedAlternatives.contradictedBy: the pool is full of real DB work, so telemetry alone does not refute it; replay does: a 64-connection pool leaves the error rate unchanged (the queue moves to the DB executor)
in-use connections are executing or queued, not idle-held
per-query execution time is flat; there are more queries, not slower ones

resolves.expected: 0 errors; p99 back to about 115 ms

partial.expected: improves slowly: the new keys have to be cached one miss at a time (entry error rate 5.7 % -> 3.6 %, p99 still about 1.1 s at the end of the window)

noEffect.expected: same error rate (the queue moves to the DB executor)
